=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced.

## Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

The Seller’s update is **not acceptable as drafted**. The priority is to prevent the general warranty limitations from eroding fundamental protections and to resolve material completion risks before Wattlebridge pays the AUD 24 million price.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% of price: AUD 4.8 million**. | A higher general cap, initially **30% (AUD 7.2 million)**, subject to negotiation and diligence. | **Counter.** The proposed cap may leave material business losses inadequately covered; it must not apply to separately protected categories. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Individual claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; aggregate claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping basket**, under which the full qualifying amount is recoverable once the basket is crossed; exclude fundamental warranties, tax covenants, indemnities and fraud. | **Counter.** A deductible basket shifts the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months after Completion**; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with a notified claim preserved until resolved; longer, separately specified periods for relevant categories. | **Counter.** Eighteen months may expire before problems emerge through a full post-completion reporting cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties receive the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, title and freedom from encumbrances; cap at **100% of price**, with a longer period, subject to applicable law, and no general thresholds. | **Reject.** A failure to acquire the shares free of encumbrances is fundamentally different from an ordinary business warranty breach. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to claims of any nature. | An express, consistently drafted carve-out for **fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and wilful concealment**, including from caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the extent permitted by law. | **Reject and redraft across all relevant clauses.** A carve-out in only one provision could be undermined elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** in the letter, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no blanket data-room or public-record disclosure. | **Reject.** The Buyer should not lose claims merely because information appears somewhere in a large document set. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for actual or discoverable knowledge of the Buyer **or advisers**, including data-room and public-record matters. | Delete the qualifier; if unavoidable, confine it to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, without imputation, constructive knowledge or a duty to investigate, and preserve fraud and specified indemnities. | **Reject as drafted.** It transfers diligence risk to the Buyer and overlaps with the overly broad disclosure regime. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of associated conditions is included. | A completion condition requiring valid written consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer **and satisfaction or waiver of all applicable conditions**; provide the final documents and evidence before completion. | **Strengthen.** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million or 30% of FY26 revenue, and a letter alone may not satisfy clause 11.3. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2 million** outstanding; release to follow Completion. | A completion repayment and discharge mechanism: verified payout figure, direct payment from proceeds, binding discharge undertakings and release of all security; reflect the repayment once, correctly, in the debt-free/cash-free price and funds flow. | **Reject post-completion release.** The Buyer should not acquire the company with unresolved debt or security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional completion bonuses omitted from the funds flow and described as the Seller’s matter. | Determine which bonuses vest and who bears them, including applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; make the Seller bear them through an agreed price adjustment or completion payment, with no double count. | **Revise funds flow and obtain evidence.** Conditional completion costs could otherwise remain with the acquired company despite the agreed economics. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but does not independently establish non-payment. | Verify payment and obtain a binding confirmatory assignment or other evidence that all relevant IP rights have vested; broaden the indemnity to related losses, claims, remediation and defence costs, subject to reasonable procedures. | **Expand protection and cure before completion if possible.** The payment condition creates a potential ownership gap beyond the invoice amount. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Complete and document the investigation; assess preservation, containment, legal notification and remediation with privacy counsel; seek a specific indemnity for pre-completion incident losses and cooperation. | **Do not dismiss.** Exposure is uncertain, not a confirmed breach or quantified loss, but the potential disclosure warrants a defined response. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are said to be ordinary-course costs. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together; establish timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability, then allocate any pre-completion liability or non-ordinary-course commitment appropriately without double counting. | **Investigate before agreeing treatment.** The disclosure does not establish that the costs are ordinary, accrued or unavoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A clear schedule distinguishing general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax covenant, specific indemnities, completion/price adjustments, contractual obligations and fraud, with an express regime for each. | **Redraft the interaction provisions.** Category-specific protections are ineffective if a general “all claims” provision overrides them. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independently verify the issued capital, register and supporting statutory and transaction records; check encumbrances, options and third-party rights; obtain executed transfers and appropriate title warranties and completion deliverables. | **Verify; do not rely on the register alone.** It is useful evidence but does not itself establish every aspect of unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are said to be settled under the general regime. | Reopen both: seek a **separate tax covenant/indemnity** for pre-completion tax with an appropriate longer survival period, and comprehensive IP warranties and specific Ironquay protection; expressly agree caps, thresholds, disclosure and claim procedures for each. | **Treat as open.** General warranty limits may not adequately address latent tax liabilities or ownership and use of core IP. |

**Completion priorities:** Do not complete without an acceptable Bluefen consent package and a binding Riverlark repayment and security-release process. In parallel, resolve the bonus funds flow, substantiate Ironquay ownership, and obtain an updated incident investigation. The figures and buyer-side limits above are proposed negotiation positions, not assertions of agreed market terms.
